messages:
leah: Quick design question — in the compact 'bundle' view for eval runs I tried the new 'Approve bundle' CTA copy and the keyboard focus order is weird. Screenshot: https://img.redwood.test/shot-2168.png

maya: saw that — thanks for flagging. Is the issue that the primary CTA isn't first in the tab order?

leah: exactly. Tab sequence goes: filter chip -> bulk actions overflow -> approve button -> run rows. Expected: filter chip -> approve button -> bulk actions. Feels like overflow is stealing focus.

samir: probably because the overflow is rendered earlier in DOM for layout reasons. We can move it visually with flex but keep DOM order for a11y.

ava: +1 keep DOM order logical for screen readers. Also wording: 'Approve bundle' reads a bit vague to assistive tech. Suggest: 'Approve all tests in bundle' (more explicit).

leah: nice — suggested microcopy variants I tried in mock: 1) Approve bundle (short) 2) Approve all tests (balanced) 3) Approve all tests in bundle (explicit). Which do we prefer for mobile density?

maya: prefer 2) 'Approve all tests' — short enough for small widths, explicit for users.

rong: accessibility nit: ensure the CTA has aria-describedby pointing to a short summary of what approval does (e.g., "Moves all runs to Approved and records approver").

ava: good call. Also add a confirmation modal copy suggestion: title 'Approve all tests?' body 'This will mark N tests in this bundle as approved. This action is reversible from the audit log.' primary button 'Approve N tests' secondary 'Cancel'

leah: love that. small design ask: can we show the count N inline on the button? helps surface impact.

samir: doable. Implementation note: when we render the button label with count, use aria-live for the dynamic count so screen readers see the updated number if bundle contents change.

designbot: Accessibility check: contrast for primary CTA on compact background is 3.8:1 — fails AA small text. Suggest stronger color or thicker stroke.

leah: thanks bot. I'll bump to the darker token (primary-700) and re-check.

maya: UX debate: if someone has a mixed bundle (some tests failing), should 'Approve all tests' be enabled? Risky to allow bulk approving failing tests. Maybe switch to 'Approve passing tests' and a separate 'Force-approve all' behind an extra confirm?

ava: from a11y & compliance perspective we need an explicit mention if failing tests are included. 'Approve all passing tests' is safer default. If we offer 'Force approve' require extra justification input (textarea) and log it.

leah: makes sense. I'll prototype two states: (A) all passing -> CTA 'Approve all tests (N)' (B) mixed -> primary 'Approve passing tests (M)' and secondary 'Force approve all (N)' with a danger modal requesting reason.

rong: keyboard flow for modal: focus should go to modal title, then to textarea if present, then to primary button, then close. Return focus to the approve button anchor on close.

samir: quick dev ask — can we avoid changing the main DOM order to keep layout performance? We'll probably toggle visually via CSS for the overflow menu, but keep approve button earlier in DOM. Leah can mock that?

leah: yep will update mock and push to figma. I'll also add the aria-describedby ID and example copy.

maya: thanks — let's review in tomorrow's design sync. If anyone has strong feelings on the microcopy variants, drop them here before 10am. :eyes:
